name: Learn: Custom Resources (CRDs)
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration and Security. Drill EVERY CRD corner harder than the exam: author a typed CRD, create and inspect CRs, discover an installed CRD, list via plural/short name, enforce schema validation (required + enum), cluster-scoped CRDs, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a CRD that won't serve. Graded exactly, per requirement.
description: Seven strict CRD practicals. Each Check shows which requirements you met and the exact reason for any you missed.

questions.title: Author a typed CustomResourceDefinition
questions.teach:
A **CustomResourceDefinition** teaches the API server a new kind. In `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` you set `spec.group`, `spec.names` (kind/plural/singular), `spec.scope`, and a `versions[]` entry with `served`/`storage` and an `openAPIV3Schema` typing the fields.

**Gotcha:** `metadata.name` MUST be exactly `<plural>.<group>` (`widgets.stable.example.com`) — any other name is rejected.
questions.prompt:
Create a CRD for a namespaced kind `Widget` in group `stable.example.com` (plural `widgets`, singular `widget`), version `v1` (served and storage), whose schema types `spec.size` (integer) and `spec.color` (string).

Target: `kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com` exists, scope Namespaced, and its `Established` condition is `True`.
questions.hint: Apply an `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` CustomResourceDefinition. `metadata.name` = `<plural>.<group>` = `widgets.stable.example.com`. Under `spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema` set `type: object` with `properties.spec` an object having `size` (integer) and `color` (string).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    kind: Widget
    plural: widgets
    singular: widget
    shortNames: [wg]
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              size: { type: integer }
              color: { type: string }
YAML
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'

verification.description: CRD widgets.stable.example.com: Namespaced, spec.size:integer + spec.color:string, Established

questions.title: Create a custom resource
questions.teach:
Once a CRD is Established you create its custom resources like any native object with `kubectl apply`. The CR's `kind` is the CRD's `names.kind` (`Widget`) and its `spec` must match the schema. A Namespaced CRD's CRs live in a namespace.

**Gotcha:** the CR's `apiVersion` is `<group>/<version>` (`stable.example.com/v1`), NOT `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` — that belongs to the CRD, not the CR.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `crd-learn`, create a `Widget` named `gadget` with `spec.size: 3` and `spec.color: blue`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget` exists with `.spec.size == 3` and `.spec.color == blue`.
questions.hint: `apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1`, `kind: Widget`, `metadata.name: gadget`, `spec.size: 3`, `spec.color: blue`. Apply into `-n crd-learn`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: gadget
spec:
  size: 3
  color: blue
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}/{.spec.color}'

verification.description: Widget 'gadget' in crd-learn with size=3 color=blue

questions.title: Discover a CRD already on the cluster
questions.teach:
On real clusters operators install their own CRDs you must discover blind: `kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com` lists the kinds, and `kubectl get crd gizmos.demo.example.com -o yaml` reveals the schema. Then create CRs against the discovered group/version.

**Gotcha:** a CR's `apiVersion` is the group plus the version where `served: true` (`demo.example.com/v1`) — read it off the CRD, don't guess.
questions.prompt:
Setup already installed a CRD for kind `Gizmo` in group `demo.example.com` (plural `gizmos`, namespaced, `spec.power` integer). Discover it, then create a `Gizmo` named `turbo` in `crd-learn` with `spec.power: 9`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get gizmo turbo` exists with `.spec.power == 9`.
questions.hint: Find it: `kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com`. Inspect: `kubectl get crd gizmos.demo.example.com -o yaml`. Then apply a `demo.example.com/v1` `Gizmo` with `spec.power: 9`.
questions.solution:
kubectl api-resources --api-group=demo.example.com
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: demo.example.com/v1
kind: Gizmo
metadata:
  name: turbo
spec:
  power: 9
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get gizmo turbo -o jsonpath='{.spec.power}'

verification.description: Gizmo 'turbo' (seeded CRD) in crd-learn with power=9

questions.title: List CRs by plural and short name
questions.teach:
A CRD registers a real kind, so its CRs list with the same verbs as native objects: `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` (plural), `get widget` (singular), and `get wg` (short name) all return the same objects.

**Gotcha:** for a Namespaced CRD, omitting `-n` lists only the current namespace — resources can look "empty" when they really exist elsewhere.
questions.prompt:
Create a **second** Widget named `widget2` in `crd-learn` (`spec.size: 7`, `spec.color: red`), so `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` shows two Widgets.

Target: namespace `crd-learn` contains at least two Widgets, including `widget2` (size=7, color=red).
questions.hint: Same shape as step 2 but `metadata.name: widget2`, `size: 7`, `color: red`. Verify with `kubectl -n crd-learn get wg` (the short name).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: widget2
spec:
  size: 7
  color: red
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get wg

verification.description: crd-learn has >=2 Widgets including widget2 (size=7 color=red)

questions.title: Schema validation: required field + enum
questions.teach:
An `openAPIV3Schema` enforces data: `required: [model]` rejects CRs missing that field, and `enum: [eco, turbo]` rejects any other value. The API server validates on apply, so a bad CR fails fast with a clear error.

**Gotcha:** the seeded `Robot` CRD requires `spec.model` and restricts `spec.mode` to `eco`/`turbo` — a CR missing `model` or using `mode: fast` is rejected; your CR must satisfy both.
questions.prompt:
Setup installed a namespaced CRD `robots.demo.example.com` (kind `Robot`) whose schema **requires** `spec.model` (string) and restricts `spec.mode` to the enum `eco` or `turbo`. Create a valid `Robot` named `r2d2` in `crd-learn` with `spec.model: astromech` and `spec.mode: turbo`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get robot r2d2` exists with `.spec.model == astromech` and `.spec.mode == turbo`.
questions.hint: Inspect the schema with `kubectl get crd robots.demo.example.com -o yaml`. Apply a `demo.example.com/v1` `Robot` with `spec.model: astromech` and `spec.mode: turbo` (both required/valid-enum).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: demo.example.com/v1
kind: Robot
metadata:
  name: r2d2
spec:
  model: astromech
  mode: turbo
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get robot r2d2 -o jsonpath='{.spec.model}/{.spec.mode}'

verification.description: Robot 'r2d2' in crd-learn with model=astromech, mode=turbo (passed required+enum validation)

questions.title: Cluster-scoped CRD
questions.teach:
`spec.scope` is either `Namespaced` or `Cluster`. A **Cluster**-scoped CRD's CRs live outside any namespace — you create and get them without `-n`, and `metadata.namespace` is ignored.

**Gotcha:** scope is fixed at creation; you cannot flip a CRD from Namespaced to Cluster later. `kubectl get <plural> -A` won't help for cluster-scoped kinds — just `kubectl get <plural>`.
questions.prompt:
Create a **Cluster**-scoped CRD for kind `Region` in group `stable.example.com` (plural `regions`, singular `region`, version `v1` served+storage, schema types `spec.zone` as string). Then create a cluster-scoped `Region` named `us-east` with `spec.zone: iad`.

Target: CRD `regions.stable.example.com` has scope `Cluster` and is Established; `kubectl get region us-east` exists with `.spec.zone == iad`.
questions.hint: In the CRD set `spec.scope: Cluster`. `metadata.name` = `regions.stable.example.com`. Create the `Region` CR with NO namespace: `kubectl get region us-east` (no `-n`).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: regions.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Cluster
  names:
    kind: Region
    plural: regions
    singular: region
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              zone: { type: string }
YAML
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/regions.stable.example.com --timeout=30s
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Region
metadata:
  name: us-east
spec:
  zone: iad
YAML
kubectl get region us-east -o jsonpath='{.spec.zone}'

verification.description: CRD regions.stable.example.com scope=Cluster Established; Region us-east with zone=iad

questions.title: Diagnose & fix: a CRD that won't serve
questions.teach:
A CRD can be installed and Established yet still refuse to create CRs when its only version has `served: false` — the REST endpoint isn't exposed, so `kubectl apply` fails with `the server could not find the requested resource`. Flip that version's `served` to `true`.

**Gotcha:** `served` and `storage` are independent per-version flags; a version can be the storage version but still be unserved. Patch the CRD, don't recreate it.
questions.prompt:
Setup installed a namespaced CRD `sprockets.demo.example.com` (kind `Sprocket`, `spec.teeth` integer), but creating a `Sprocket` fails. Diagnose why and fix the CRD so its `v1` is served, then create a `Sprocket` named `sp1` in `crd-learn` with `spec.teeth: 12`. Do not delete and recreate the CRD — patch it.

Target: CRD `sprockets.demo.example.com` version `v1` has `served: true`, and `kubectl -n crd-learn get sprocket sp1` exists with `.spec.teeth == 12`.
questions.hint: `kubectl get crd sprockets.demo.example.com -o yaml` → `versions[0].served: false`. Patch it: `kubectl patch crd sprockets.demo.example.com --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/versions/0/served","value":true}]'`. Then apply the `demo.example.com/v1` `Sprocket` with `spec.teeth: 12`.
questions.solution:
# The only version has served:false, so no REST endpoint exists for Sprocket.
kubectl patch crd sprockets.demo.example.com --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/versions/0/served","value":true}]'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/sprockets.demo.example.com --timeout=30s
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: demo.example.com/v1
kind: Sprocket
metadata:
  name: sp1
spec:
  teeth: 12
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get sprocket sp1 -o jsonpath='{.spec.teeth}'

verification.description: sprockets CRD v1 served=true; Sprocket sp1 in crd-learn with teeth=12
